To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(1) Malate degradation was rapid (t½ = 1.7 hours) in all soils studied and (2) Malate uptake was energy-dependent and was not limited by nitrogen in mixed bacterial cultures.
the breakdown of organic acids in acid soils is rapid, and that the breakdown is not inhibited by low pH.

(1) root exudation is an important mechanism of Al detoxification, (2) Al toxicity is not the only stress that can cause root exudation, (3) the kinetics of root exudation and the kinetics of root uptake of organic acids are very similar, (4) the kinetics of malate decomposition in soils are very similar to the kinetics of malic acid uptake by bacteria, (5) root exudate is a major source of organic acids in acid soils,
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of microorganisms in the breakdown of organic acids in acid soils.
the role of root exudates in the rhizosphere and the impact of microorganisms on the fate of these compounds.
the effect of soil acidity and soil microorganisms on the root exudation and breakdown of malate in acid soils.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the microbial populations in the soil are not the limiting factor in malate breakdown in acid soils, but that the breakdown is rapid and the organic acid is a major source of carbon and energy for soil microorganisms.
root exudation is not a viable strategy in acid soils.
root exudation is not the only source of organic acids in acid soils.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
root exudation in response to Al stress is unlikely to be a major factor in Al tolerance in the acid soils we have examined.
in the presence of Al stress the root release of malate will not only be a function of the Al concentration but also the microbial population in the rhizosphere.

in acid soils where microbial populations are large, root exudation is a futile exercise for root mediated Al resistance mechanisms as the organic acid will be rapidly degraded by the soil microorganisms.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the microbial populations are capable of rapidly taking up and decomposing organic acids in soil and that the microbial populations can compete for organic acids with the roots.
root exudation may not be a very effective strategy for Al resistance in acidic soils, and that the root may be a better sink for Al than a source.
organic acids are rapidly metabolized by microbes in acid soils and the kinetics of the breakdown are independent of the pH of the soil.
